identity_note: Both official guide pages have an inconsistent template field saying District16. statements.claim: Lists expanded Medicare for All first in the guide's explicit Top Three Issues section.

Includes housing as a right in her economic- and social-dignity agenda.

statements.claim: States that rejecting corporate PAC and lobbyist contributions allows prioritizing working-class families. No independent finance audit is inferred.
Criticizes Democrats for accepting high rents, expensive healthcare and underfunded education, and argues faster change requires political courage.
Lists healthcare first in the same Top Three Issues format; does not specify an insurance model in that item.

comparisons.analysis: Both explicitly list healthcare as their first issue. Ocasio-Cortez names expanded Medicare for All; Crowley's short priority item does not specify an insurance mechanism.
Ocasio-Cortez explicitly calls for ICE abolition, while Crowley promises comprehensive immigration reform. The latter's unspecified agency policy is not coded as opposition to abolition.

Ocasio-Cortez criticizes Democrats settling for inadequate outcomes and emphasizes political courage; Crowley promises congressional action for working families. This compares their stated framing without inferring unspoken policy disagreement.
